full_judgment:
3. The plaintiff’s case, in brief, is that the suit land originally belonged to one Paimullah Kabiraj and he died leaving behind four sons and two daughters. The plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest Kali Kumar Pal; purchased the suit land from the said heirs of Paimullah Kabiraj by registered deed No. 1406 dated 24.3.42 It is also the case of the plaintiff that during the SA Operation the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiff and some of the defendants. Thereafter the plaintiff filed a case before the revenue authority under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. After hearing, plaintiff's case was allowed and the defendants names were struck out and the name of the sole plaintiff was substituted in the record of right by order dated 24.6.75 passed by the Additional Circle Officer, Revenue, Parbatipur. The plaintiff further asserted that he has althrough been in possession of the suit land since purchased in the year 1951 and before that their predecessor-in-interest had been in possession of the land. 

 21. Admittedly he was a Korfa tenant but if the suit is transferred without the consent of the landlord, the landlord may take over the possession under section 48 (f) of the Bengal Tenancy Act but it does not appear that the landlord has so taken over the possession of the suit land. The Korfa tenant or his heirs cannot challenge their own transfer.
